introduction: This is part two of our video series on the history of Napoleon. In this video, we cover the period

vocabulary.definition: a temporary alliance of distinct parties, persons, or states for joint action
vocabulary.example: Russia and Austria formed a new anti-French coalition to oppose Napoleon.
The Spanish armada set sail to challenge the British naval forces.

vocabulary.definition: a member of a small independent group taking part in irregular fighting, typically against larger regular forces
vocabulary.example: The Spanish militias employed guerrilla tactics against the occupying French army.

vocabulary.definition: to add or attach a territory to an existing political unit such as a country
vocabulary.example: Prussia's western territories were annexed to the Kingdom of Westphalia as per the peace treaty.

vocabulary.definition: information, especially biased or misleading in nature, used to promote a political cause or point of view
vocabulary.example: Napoleon censored the media and spread propaganda to control the narrative.

vocabulary.definition: a formal agreement between warring parties to temporarily stop fighting, typically to discuss peace terms
vocabulary.example: After days of fighting, the Austrians retreated and asked for an armistice with Napoleon.
